Drawer size: single-view measure_box_on_table is ambiguous between height and length (unconstrained fit gave h=4 cm); height bounded 0.10-0.15 m from the front-face pixel height, then a scale fit through video_cam (0.94) set the final 11.3 x 25.4 x 10.3 cm.
The drawer unit is a free body (the task never moves the housing); its tray joint is closed at frame 0.

The toy is Stage 1 'deformable' (soft plush): reconstructed as a compliant MuJoCo body plus an Isaac Sim compliant soft body; the Isaac copy settles with 0.04 mm drift but turns 17 deg as its ellipsoids settle into the compliant contact.
Travel 0.203 m (0.8 x depth) is the physical limit for a tray that stays in the housing; Stage 1 described it as roughly one housing length.

Maintainer rebuild (release examples): Stage 3's end_state_rest_audit found the first-pass plush (construct_plush_toy, condim 4) rocking in the closed drawer for seconds (13 deg about its long axis at 2.5 Hz, still 10 deg after 3 s, touching only the tray floor): a body of ellipsoids on a flat floor has nothing that resists rolling. Rebuilt with construct_plush_toy_rolling (new: the same toy with condim 6, torsional friction 1 cm and rolling friction 5 mm, the contact patch of a squashed plush) and proven with drop_rest_test (new); same size, mass, colour, softness and placement; the scene was re-staged from setup/scene.xml (which now carries the hand hull collision geoms) at the first pass's fitted poses and every MuJoCo check re-run. The Isaac soft-body copy (isaac/) is the first pass's: its PhysX compliant material does not use the MuJoCo rolling friction, and isaac_export_check passes on the new scene.
